vshift.description: Reference value for the zero-equivalent value of the absolute value.

post_gamma.description: Standard gamma correction applied to the elevation values. This is a monotonic power-law remapping that shifts emphasis toward low or high elevations, making the overall shape sharper or bulkier without changing its ordering.

post_remap.description: Linearly remaps the output values to a specified target range (default is [0, 1]).
post_remap.label: Remap Range

post_saturate.description: Modifies the amplitude of elevations by first clamping them to a given interval and then scaling them so that the restricted interval matches the original input range. This enhances contrast in elevation variations while maintaining overall structure.
post_saturate.label: Saturation Range

post_smoothing_radius.description: Defines the radius for post-processing smoothing, determining the size of the neighborhood used to average local values and reduce high-frequency detail. A radius of 0 disables smoothing.

vshift.description: Reference value for the zero-equivalent value of the absolute value.

octaves.description: The number of octaves for fractal noise generation. More octaves add finer details to the terrain.

persistence.description: The amplitude scaling factor for subsequent noise octaves. Lower values reduce the contribution of higher octaves.

post_gamma.description: Standard gamma correction applied to the elevation values. This is a monotonic power-law remapping that shifts emphasis toward low or high elevations, making the overall shape sharper or bulkier without changing its ordering.

post_smoothing_radius.description: Defines the radius for post-processing smoothing, determining the size of the neighborhood used to average local values and reduce high-frequency detail. A radius of 0 disables smoothing.

seed.description: Random seed number. The random seed is an offset to the randomized process. A different seed will produce a new result.

warp0.description: Initial warp scale applied at the first octave (Jordan variant); controls how strongly the noise gradients displace subsequent octaves.

HydraulicParticle.description: HydraulicParticle is a particle-based hydraulic erosion operator that simulates the erosion and sediment transport processes that occur due to the flow of water over a terrain represented by the input heightmap. This type of operator models erosion by tracking the movement of virtual particles (or sediment particles) as they are transported by water flow and interact with the terrain. Erosion is gradient-driven: flat or masked-to-zero input has no slope and produces little or no change. Erode full-domain relief first, then multiply by the land mask.
HydraulicParticle.label: HydraulicParticle

bd_elevation_strength.description: Controls elevation-based bedrock offset. Increases allowable erosion depth proportionally to elevation relative to the terrain height range, enabling deeper erosion at higher altitudes while protecting lowlands.

bd_slope.description: Slope threshold for slope-based bedrock resistance. Areas steeper than this slope limit have less erosion allowance to preserve steep cliff formations.

bd_slope_strength.description: Controls slope-based bedrock offset. Deepens the bedrock on flatter surfaces below the slope limit, protecting steep cliff faces from over-erosion.
bd_slope_strength.label: Bedrock Slope Gap

c_inertia.description: Particle inertia factor: how strongly a particle keeps its current direction instead of following the local gradient. Higher values produce longer, straighter erosion paths.

collapse_rate.description: Rate of bank collapse and talus relaxation. Controls how much steep bank material collapses into the channel when slopes exceed the talus limit.

enable_default_bedrock.description: Generates an automatic bedrock heightmap when no bedrock input is connected, limiting maximum erosion depth based on elevation and slope.

enable_ridge_forcing.description: Enables ridge forcing during multiscale erosion: an added large-scale ridge pattern that steers particles and accentuates ridge lines.

aspect_strength.description: Weighting factor scaling snow melt rates based on solar aspect orientation.

SnowSimulation.description: Simulates snow accumulation, wind drift redistribution, creeping downhill deformation, and ablation.

clamp_min_ratio.description: Lower relative threshold ratio clipping insignificant snow depths.
clamp_min_ratio.label: Lower Threshold Ratio

depth_map_type.description: Selects the method or source used to compute initial water or snow depth.

k_creep.description: Creep coefficient governing downhill viscous deformation of snowpack.

outflow_boundaries.description: Allows water or snow to freely drain across external domain boundaries.

WaterDepthDryOut.description: Reduces (dries out) the water depth by applying a ratio to the input depth. This can be used to simulate evaporation, infiltration, or partial drying of flooded areas. An optional mask can be provided to control where the drying effect is applied.
WaterDepthDryOut.label: WaterDepthDryOut

dry_out_ratio.description: Ratio applied to the input depth to reduce water. A value of 0 removes all water, while 1 keeps the original depth.
dry_out_ratio.label: dry_out_ratio

mask.caption: mask
mask.description: Optional mask defining where the drying effect is applied. Unmasked areas remain unchanged.

water_depth.caption: water_depth
water_depth.description: Output water depth map representing flooded areas.

WaterDepthFromMask.description: Computes water depth over a terrain using a mask to define flooded regions. The method performs a harmonic interpolation (Laplace equation) over the masked domain using a Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR) solver. The resulting water surface is interpolated from boundary conditions, and the water depth is obtained as the difference between this surface and the terrain elevation.
WaterDepthFromMask.label: WaterDepthFromMask

iterations.description: Maximum number of SOR iterations used to solve the harmonic interpolation.
iterations.label: Max Iterations

mask_threshold.description: Threshold used to convert the input mask into a binary field. Values above the threshold define flooded regions, while lower values act as boundaries.
mask_threshold.label: Mask Activation Threshold

tolerance.description: Convergence tolerance. The solver stops when the maximum update between iterations falls below this value.
tolerance.label: Convergence Tolerance

water_depth.caption: water_depth
water_depth.description: Output water depth map representing flooded areas.

water_mask.caption: water_mask
water_mask.description: Input mask defining where water can accumulate. Values above the threshold indicate flooded regions.

WaterElevationFromDepth.description: Computes the absolute water elevation by adding the terrain elevation and the water depth. This simplifies workflows where only depth is available. The resulting water elevation can be used, for example, when exporting water as an asset with ExportAsset.
WaterElevationFromDepth.label: WaterElevationFromDepth

water_depth.caption: water_depth
water_depth.description: Output water depth map representing flooded areas.

water_elevation.caption: water_elevation
water_elevation.description: Output absolute water elevation computed as elevation + water_depth.

WaterMask.description: Computes a gradient-based water mask using an extended water-depth model. This produces a smooth mask indicating regions that become flooded when water depth is artificially increased by a specified amount. It can also be used to generate a transition mask between water and ground, useful for effects such as texturing a sand beach.
WaterMask.label: WaterMask

additional_depth.description: Amount of additional water depth used to simulate how water would further spread over the terrain.
additional_depth.label: Additional Water Depth
